proposal: Add a season-end `breaks` block to the `tennis:tour` coverage contract in scripts/config/authority.json so the dead November tail after the ATP/WTA Tour finals stops firing a FALSE HIGH contract breach every pipeline run. The regular tour ends with its season finales mid-November (WTA Finals Riyadh 14.11, ATP Finals Torino 22.11 — Alcaraz won, in RSS), but the contract's `months` list holds all of November in-season; with the tour over, `upcoming` is legitimately 0, so coverage-contracts.js scored tennis:tour 'breached' and coverage-gaps lifted it to a HIGH contract-breach gap on every run from ~23 Nov onward — even though coverage is correct and complete (there is simply nothing to board). December is already off-season (outside `months`), so the only false-breach window is the post-finals November tail. The fix mirrors the EXACT remedy already in this file for the PGA-Tour ~2.5-week autumn pause and the Eliteserien/PL FIFA-landslagspauser: a documented, legitimate pause that whole-calendar-month `months` cannot model, suppressed with a dated `breaks` window (status 'break', never 'breached'). Added 2026-11-23→30 (firmly evidenced) plus a 2027-11-22→30 forward projection (ATP Finals Torino ~mid-Nov 2027) so it does not silently re-break next season, with a note to refine when the 2027 calendar firms up.

Uten fiks triageres det falske bruddet hver kjøring (agent-triage/G2-støy schemaet ber oss unngå). improve/self-repair-sak.'

Live docs/data/coverage-contracts.json (generatedAt 2026-11-23T15:40:31Z) confirms the firing bug: tennis:tour { inSeason true, upcoming 0, status 'breached' } and the top-level breached array = ['tennis:tour']. This is the ONLY breach in the file — every other contract is 'met'/'off-season'/'break'. The breach feeds coverage-gaps' contract-breach signal (always HIGH severity, WP-243) as recurring G2 noise.

coverage-audit.json notes[3] 'FALSKT KONTRAKTBRUDD (WP-243)' documents that it is a season-end miscalibration not a real gap: 'den regulære ATP/WTA-touren er over (ATP Finals 22. nov, WTA Finals 14. nov), neste tour-event ~sent des. ... Davis Cup Finals (24.–29., uten Norge) tatt med som LOW.' Davis Cup Finals is a tier2 TEAM event, not the regular tour the contract measures, and has no tracked Norwegian (Ruud's Norway only played Davis Cup qualies) — so there is genuinely nothing for the tour contract to board in the tail, making 'break' the honest state.

The `breaks` mechanism is exactly the documented tool for this class: scripts/lib/coverage-contracts.js (isWithinBreak) and authority.schema.json already support it; the Eliteserien (football:eliteserien) and Premier League (football:premier-league) contracts in the same authority.json use dated `breaks` for the FIFA-landslagspauser (2026-09-21→10-06, 2026-11-09→17, 2027-...), and golf:pga-tour widened horizonDays to 21 for its autumn pause — all added by prior improve runs for the identical 'months cannot model a sub-month gap' failure. This change reuses that mechanism; it adds NO new machinery (the improve bias).

Verified the fix with the real data: re-running assessContracts(authority, events.json, now) after the edit returns tennis:tour { status 'break', upcoming 0, inSeason true, inBreak true } and breached = [] — the false breach is gone, while the mechanism (status still transparently reported, off-season still wins, malformed windows fail-soft) is unchanged and already unit-tested in tests/coverage-contracts.test.js.

expectedEffect: From the next static-pipeline run, coverage-contracts.json scores tennis:tour 'break' (not 'breached') through 23–30 Nov 2026 (and 22–30 Nov 2027), so the breached array drops tennis:tour, coverage-gaps stops emitting the HIGH contract-breach gap for it, and the contracts port in port-report.json stops counting a false breach against G2. One recurring false positive that two+ agents have re-triaged every run disappears, with zero loss of real-gap sensitivity (early/mid-November tour events still count; December is unchanged off-season; a genuinely dead tennis fetcher during an in-season, non-break week still breaches).

notes: Scope deliberately minimal: only the evidenced season-end tail. Did NOT touch `months` (removing November would make the whole month off-season and hide a REAL gap during the early/mid-November tour weeks — Paris Masters, the finals themselves — exactly the over-correction the file's own notes warn against). The break window is the precise, documented fix the audit asked for.
